_meta.hadith: s7b prostration today only to Allah: Ibn Majah 1853
_meta.status: v2 06.11.2026 – H55/H60 + ChatGPT H52: verses quoted complete (12:15, 19, 22, 38, 42, 55, 58, 90, 91, 92, 93, 100, 101) or told in Oma's words without verse marks (12:4, 8, 10, 21, 23, 33, 47–49, 94); removed «طيّب», «all food stores», «in Yaqub's land», «allowed then as greeting» (kept: today we prostrate only to Allah); 12:76 as «Allah's plan»

open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Noah… Ilyas… Do you remember the vision Yusuf saw in his sleep? Eleven stars, the sun and the moon… he saw them bowing down to him. Today you will finally find out what this vision means!
s1c: Exactly that. Get warm and cosy… Today I’ll tell you about the Prophet Yusuf, peace be upon him. His story has a whole surah in the Qur’an named after him: Surah Yusuf.
s2a: Yusuf’s brothers were jealous of him. They said that Yusuf and his brother were dearer to their father than they were. And they wanted to send Yusuf away. One of them said: Throw him into the bottom of the well, perhaps some travellers will pick him up.
s2b: Allah says: “So when they took him and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well… But We inspired to him, ‘You will surely inform them someday about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive.’” That means: one day you will tell them what they did. Then He says: “And there came a company of travelers; then they sent their water drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, ‘Good news! Here is a boy.’ And they concealed him, taking him as merchandise; and Allah was knowing of what they did.”
s2c: Alhamdulillah! Did they take him back home?
s2d: No, my dear. They sold him for a small price, a few coins. A man from Egypt bought him and told his wife to treat him kindly, perhaps he would benefit them or they would adopt him as a son. And Allah says: “And when Joseph reached maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge. And thus We reward the doers of good.”
s3a: Yusuf grew up and became a young man. One day, the wife of the master of the house wanted him to do something Allah had forbidden. But Yusuf said: I seek refuge in Allah! And he hurried to the door. She pulled his shirt from behind, and it tore.
s3b: From behind? And why is that important?
s3c: Good question! A man from her own family said: If his shirt was torn from behind, then Yusuf is the truthful one, because he was running away. And that’s exactly how it was! Even so, Yusuf was put in prison. He had prayed to his Lord that prison was dearer to him than what they were calling him to.
s4a: In the prison there were two young men. Each of them saw a dream, and they asked Yusuf what it meant. Yusuf first said: “And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And it was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the favor of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.” And after that he explained their dreams.
s4b: He told the first one: You will go free and serve drink to your master again. For the other one, the dream had a sad meaning. Allah says: “And he said to the one whom he knew would go free, ‘Mention me before your master.’ But Satan made him forget the mention to his master, and Joseph remained in prison several years.” That means: Yusuf asked him to tell his master about him, but he forgot.
s4c: Several years? That’s a long time!
s5a: Then the king of Egypt had a strange dream: seven fat cows were eaten by seven thin cows. And he saw seven green ears of grain, and others that were dry. No one could explain the dream. Then the man who had been in prison finally remembered Yusuf!
s5b: Yusuf explained the dream and said: Plant for seven years, and whatever you harvest, leave it in its ears, except a little that you eat. Then seven hard years will come, in which you will eat what you saved. Then after that a year will come in which the people get rain.
s5c: The king said: Bring Yusuf to me! But Yusuf said: First it must be shown that I am innocent. And indeed, the wife of the master of the house admitted that Yusuf had told the truth. Then Yusuf said: “Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian.” And so Allah gave Yusuf a strong position in the land.
s6a: Then the hard years came. Allah says: “And the brothers of Joseph came, and they entered upon him; and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown.” That means: Yusuf recognized them, but they did not recognize him!
s6b: They had no idea it was Yusuf!
s6c: With Allah’s plan, Yusuf kept his brother with him. And when the brothers came back to him, they finally recognized him: “They said, ‘Are you indeed Joseph?’ He said, ‘I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who fears Allah and is patient, then indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.’”
s6d: “They said, ‘By Allah, certainly has Allah preferred you over us, and indeed, we have been sinners.’” And what did Yusuf say? “He said, ‘No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful.’”
s6e: He just forgave them? After everything they did?
s6f: Yes, my dear. Forgiving is sometimes harder than anything else. And that is exactly what Yusuf did.
s7a: Then Yusuf said: “Take this, my shirt, and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing. And bring me your family, all together.” When the caravan left Egypt, Yaqub said that he could smell Yusuf! They laid the shirt on his face, and Yaqub could see again!
s7b: And the whole family came to Egypt. Allah says: “And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, ‘O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you here from bedouin life after Satan had induced estrangement between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.’” But we today prostrate only to Allah.
s7c: The eleven stars were the brothers! And the sun and the moon were the parents!
s7d: Exactly, my clever one. And Yusuf prayed to his Lord: “My Lord, You have given me something of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.”
s8a: Oh… they’ve fallen asleep. My dears… be honest like Yusuf, even when it is hard. Trust Allah, even when it is as dark as in a well. And forgive others, just as Yusuf forgave his brothers.
s8b: And next time, I’ll tell you about Ayyub… a prophet who became very sick and stayed patient. And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
